title: U.S. House · New Jersey's 5th District
area: Northern New Jersey, including all or part of Bergen, Passaic, and Sussex counties.

context.text: Incumbent Josh Gottheimer ran unopposed in the June 2, 2026 Democratic primary, winning 100% of the vote. Sean Kirrane won the Republican primary unopposed after Chandiha Gajapathy withdrew.
The Cook Political Report's Partisan Voter Index rates the district D+2.

summary.text: Josh Gottheimer is the Democratic incumbent for New Jersey's 5th Congressional District, first elected in 2016. He serves on the House Financial Services Committee and the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence, and co-chairs the bipartisan Problem Solvers Caucus and SALT Caucus.

background.text: Born and raised in Essex County, New Jersey; graduated from West Essex Senior High School.
Earned a bachelor's degree from the University of Pennsylvania and a law degree from Harvard Law School.
Worked as a speechwriter for President Bill Clinton, including on two State of the Union addresses, and later worked on the presidential campaigns of Wesley Clark and John Kerry.
Before running for Congress, worked at Microsoft as a general manager for corporate strategy and as senior counselor to the chairman of the Federal Communications Commission.

priorities.text: Helped launch the bipartisan Problem Solvers Caucus in 2017 and now serves as its Vice-Chair, working across party lines on taxes, the environment, healthcare affordability, national security, and infrastructure.
Co-chairs the bipartisan SALT Caucus, which pushes to restore the state and local tax deduction, and the Law Enforcement Caucus.

record.text: Serves on the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence, where he is Ranking Member of the Subcommittee on National Security Agency and Cyber and a member of the Subcommittee on Defense Intelligence and Overhead Architecture, and on the House Financial Services Committee, including its Subcommittee on National Security, Illicit Finance, and International Financial Institutions and Subcommittee on Digital Assets, Financial Technology, and Artificial Intelligence.
Announced introduction of the bipartisan Kylie's Voices for Childhood Cancer Act ("Kylie's Law") with Rep. Mike Lawler (NY-17) during Childhood Cancer Awareness Month.
Introduced the bipartisan Stop Rogue AI Act with Rep. Mike Lawler, legislation intended to establish guardrails for AI "agents" operating on computer networks.
The House passed the AM Radio for Every Vehicle Act, a bill Gottheimer says he first championed, requiring automakers to include AM radio in new vehicles.
The House passed the bipartisan, Gottheimer-led GUARD Act, aimed at protecting seniors from financial fraud and scammers.

candidates.name: Sean Kirrane
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 2, 2026 Republican primary unopposed after the withdrawal of Chandiha Gajapathy.

summary.text: Sean Kirrane is the Republican nominee for New Jersey's 5th Congressional District. An entrepreneur and healthcare/finance executive from Westwood, he describes his campaign as bringing private-sector "turnaround" management experience to a federal government he says has a "management problem," focused on affordability, healthcare, and housing.

background.text: Born in Westwood, New Jersey; earned a high school diploma from Bergen Catholic High School and a bachelor's degree from St. Joseph's University in 2000. Also attended Villanova University.
Career experience as an entrepreneur and executive; as of 2025 was affiliated with Cortex-X, the Kirrane Group, and Arcadia Health Partners.
Describes more than twenty years working in healthcare, finance and technology, including leading what he calls billion-dollar transactions and turnarounds of bankrupt hospitals.
background.quote: I've led billion-dollar transactions, rebuilt bankrupt hospitals, and turned around organizations that others had written off.

priorities.text: "Government should do fewer things — and do them well," proposing to cap administrative costs at 10% across federal programs and eliminate waste.
priorities.quote: Government should do fewer things — and do them well.

priorities.text: Housing, through what he calls the American Citizens' Primary Residence Mortgage Act to protect homeownership for U.S. citizens.
Healthcare, through what he calls the American Citizens' Health Insurance Act, which he says would guarantee affordable baseline coverage while preserving free-market choice.
Homelessness, through what he calls the Homeless Solutions and Stability Act, replacing what he describes as unsafe shelters with treatment-based recovery programs.

positions.summary: Says he would pursue a healthcare proposal guaranteeing affordable baseline coverage while preserving free-market choice, rather than expanding public coverage directly.

candidates.name: Adam Rueda

summary.text: Adam Rueda is the Humane Sustainable Future Party candidate for New Jersey's 5th Congressional District. A 28-year-old Bucknell graduate and financial analyst, he says he co-founded a new political party, "greenparty2.0," focused on environmental and health policy, gun-control reform, and campaign-finance/lobbying reform.

background.text: Raised in Andover Township (Sussex County); earned a Bachelor of Science in Business Administration, with a focus in financial management and accounting, from Bucknell University in 2019.
Has worked as a senior financial analyst at a commercial real estate brokerage in Morristown and as an interior design salesperson.

priorities.text: Says he co-founded "greenparty2.0," a party he describes as led by "Earth-first, health-first" young activists, focused on environmental and health policy.
Supports stricter gun-control measures, including reform to gun storage requirements and additional steps, such as mental-health evaluations, before purchase.

Says lobbying and campaign contributions from the fossil-fuel industry and pro-Israel groups like AIPAC improperly influence sitting members of Congress, and supports campaign-finance and election reform, including open primaries.

positions.summary: Supports stricter gun-storage requirements and additional screening, including mental-health evaluations, before firearm purchases, and wants to limit access to assault weapons.
Says the U.S. should divest from fossil fuels and move swiftly on green-energy solutions to address ecosystem degradation and intensifying storms.

candidates.researchNotes: No official campaign website located; positions drawn from his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey responses.
